results.content: Strategies to handle missing data: ✔️ Remove them – Safe if only a small fraction of rows are missing ✔️ Mean/Median imputation – For numerical features, preserves distribution ✔️ Mode imputation – Best for categorical variables (like city, gender) ✔️ Forward/Backward fill – Common in time-series datasets to keep continuity ✔️ Model-based imputation – Use ML models (e.g., regression, k-NN) to estimate missing values intelligently 💡 Example: In a house price dataset 🏠, if “lot size” is missing: ✅ Filling with the median keeps skewed distributions realistic ✅ Using a regression model with features like “number of rooms” or “neighborhood” can yield better imputations 👉 Takeaway: Missing values aren’t just a nuisance — they’re a data quality challenge. 🎯 Day 3 – Ridge vs Lasso: Regularized Machine Learning Today’s session focused on how regularization techniques improve model performance and prevent overfitting in regression models. 📊 Plotting Distributions in Machine Learning Before building any ML model, you need to understand your data — and the best way to do that is by visualizing distributions.
